summary: This standards-track document defines a Management Information Base for managing SONET/SDH circuit emulation over packet networks. The MIB lets network management tools read and configure such circuits using SNMP. It models these circuits across a packet switched network.

eli5.summary: Network tools need a dictionary of knobs and dials to check a device. This dictionary is for old telephone-style circuits carried over modern packet networks.

subtitle: The SNMP MIB module for configuring and monitoring SONET/SDH circuits that are carried across a packet network.

tldr.problem: Operators who carry SONET/SDH circuits across a packet switched network need a standard way to configure and monitor those emulated circuits from network management tools.
tldr.mechanism: The PW-CEP-STD-MIB module defines tables that tie a SONET/SDH path or virtual tributary to a pseudowire, hold shared configuration, and report performance in 15-minute and 1-day intervals. It works together with the PW-STD-MIB module.
tldr.outcome: A CEP pseudowire is set up by creating rows in a few linked tables, then watched through the performance tables. Write access needs protection, and SNMPv3 is recommended.

today: RFC 6240 is a Proposed Standard published in May 2011. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: What the CEP MIB Manages
sections.content:
RFC 6240 describes a model for managing SONET/SDH Time Division Multiplexed (TDM) digital signals that are encapsulated for transmission over a Packet Switched Network (PSN). It is closely related to RFC 4842, which describes the technology itself and the Circuit Emulation Service over a PSN.

The management model is a MIB module, PW-CEP-STD-MIB, which works with the module in RFC 5601 and the textual conventions in RFC 5542. Following RFC 2863, a CEP connection is a pseudowire (PW) and is therefore not represented in the ifTable. CEP carries structured SONET/SDH paths, so each path or Virtual Tributary (VT) can be processed separately. The section/line/path interface stack is modeled in RFC 3592.
sections.eli5: It is a control panel for sending old-style phone-line signals across a computer network. It does not redescribe how the sending works. That is in another RFC.

sections.title: Terminology and Design Goals
sections.content:
Structured emulation, as outlined in RFC 4842, terminates the SONET/SDH section and line overhead. It then breaks the path's Synchronous Payload Envelope (SPE) into fragments for the PSN. A CEP header with a sequence number and pointer adjustment information is added at the start of each fragment.

"Outbound" is the direction in which a path's payload is received, adapted to packets, given a PW label and sent into the PSN. "Inbound" is the reverse: packets arrive from the PSN and are reassembled into an SPE inserted into the SONET/SDH section and line. A path is bidirectional and symmetrical, so CEP uses the same timeslot, width and packet size both ways, though inbound and outbound PW labels may differ.

The feature checklist says the module must work with PW-STD-MIB, be independent of the PSN type, support all signal types from RFC 4842 (SPE, fractional SPE, VT, for both SONET and SDH) with all its optional features, and report all the statistics that RFC defines.
sections.eli5: Outbound means signal going into the network, inbound means coming out of it. Both directions use the same size lanes, but the labels on the packets may differ.

sections.title: Layering with the Pseudowire MIBs
sections.content:
The MIB structure for a PW service has three layers, following the PWE3 architecture in RFC 3985. The layering is meant to isolate PW services from the PSN that carries them while giving a standard way to connect any supported service to any supported PSN.

  • The service layer holds service-specific modules such as this one. They collaborate with existing MIB modules for the native service and "glue" them to the PWE3 modules.
  • The middle layer is PW-STD-MIB, which configures general PW parameters common to all emulated services and PSNs.
  • The PSN layer holds PSN-specific modules that associate a PW with one or more tunnels carrying the service over the PSN.
sections.eli5: Think of three floors: the top floor knows about the phone-line signal, the middle floor knows about pseudowires in general, and the bottom floor knows about the network underneath.

sections.title: The Tables in the Module
sections.content:
The module is built from six tables.

  • pwCepTable links a SONET/SDH path or VT (its ifIndex and timeslot) to a PW, holds the index of its configuration entry, and carries config error and status indications.
  • pwCepCfgTable holds CEP PW configuration. One entry may be shared by many pwCepTable entries when they use the same settings.
  • pwCepPerfCurrentTable has statistics for the current 15-minute period.
  • pwCepPerfIntervalTable keeps historical intervals, usually 96 15-minute entries covering 24 hours.
  • pwCepPerf1DayIntervalTable accumulates statistics for the current day and holds previous days.
  • pwCepFracTable adds configuration and monitoring for fractional SPE PWs.

The agent creates a pwCepTable entry for every PW whose pwType is 'cep', indexed by pwIndex. The type of a CEP PW is one of spe, vt or fracSpe, defaulting to spe. Support for vt and fracSpe is optional. Manual entries SHOULD be preserved after a reboot, and if a row is found inconsistent afterwards, pwOperStatus MUST be declared notPresent(5).
sections.eli5: There are six tables, like six forms. One form links a phone-line to a pseudowire, one holds settings, and the others keep score over short and long time periods.

sections.title: Configuring and Observing a CEP Pseudowire
sections.content:
Configuring a CEP PW follows four steps:

  1. Create an entry in the pwTable as defined in RFC 5601.
  2. Configure the PSN tunnel in the PSN-specific modules, then set the SONET path width in sonetPathCurrentTable and the path index and starting timeslot in pwCepTable. The agent creates the pwCepTable entry from the pwTable entry.
  3. Create an entry in pwCepCfgTable if no suitable one exists (packet length and so on), and set its index in pwCepTable.
  4. Once the PW is operational, use the three performance tables to monitor counts, indicators and conditions.
sections.eli5: First make the pseudowire, then say which phone-line it carries, then pick its settings, and last watch the gauges.

sections.title: Worked Example: An STS-3c Path
sections.content:
The RFC's example sets up an STS-3c path starting at SONET timeslot 1. In RFC 3592 terms, the sonetPathCurrentEntry has ifIndex 23 and sonetPathCurrentWidth of 3. A pwCepCfgTable entry at index 9 sets a payload length of 783 bytes, no minimum packet length, packet reordering true, a jitter buffer depth of 500 microseconds, and pwCepCfgRowStatus of createAndGo. Further values cover loss of packet synchronization (2 consecutive in-sync packets to exit, 10 missing to enter), a play-out value of 0xFF for errored packets, and severely-errored-second thresholds.

In PW-STD-MIB the operator gets a new index with pwIndexNext (here 83), creates the pwTable entry with pwType set to 'cep', and then sets pwCepSonetIfIndex to 23 and pwCepCfgIndex to 9 in the new pwCepTable entry.
sections.eli5: The example fills in the forms for one fat phone-line: it names the line, picks settings from a saved settings sheet, and links the two together.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The module can configure objects as well as monitor them, so anything that can be configured can be misconfigured, with potentially disastrous results. The read-write and read-create objects in pwCepTable, pwCepCfgTable and pwCepFracTable control CEP PW parameters on a Provider Edge (PE) device, and unauthorized access could disrupt traffic. SNMPv3 VACM and USM MUST be used with any v3 agent that implements the module.

Readable objects can also be sensitive: pwCepTable and the three performance tables together show the CEP pseudowire connectivity topology and performance. Versions of SNMP before SNMPv3 lacked adequate security, so it is RECOMMENDED to deploy SNMPv3 with cryptographic security, and deploying earlier versions is NOT RECOMMENDED. The IANA section records one value: pwCepStdMIB is { mib-2 200 }.
sections.eli5: These dials can break the network if the wrong person turns them, and the gauges show how the network is wired. So only trusted people should get in, using the strongest lock available.
